Thought: I need to compute the 2022-2023 crime change for each borough, construct a row-standardized spatial weights matrix from the adjacency list, calculate Global Moran's I, and evaluate its significance with a permutation test using at least 500 shuffles. I'll perform all of these steps in a single code block to obtain the observed statistic and p-value.

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_2022_2023_crime.csv'

# Load datasets
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Compute year-on-year change (2023 minus 2022)
df['change'] = df['Crime_2023'] - df['Crime_2022']

# Consistent borough ordering
boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].unique())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric binary adjacency matrix (cap at 1 to handle any duplicate entries)
W_bin = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = str(row['borough']).strip()
    b2 = str(row['neighbor']).strip()
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W_bin[i, j] = 1
        W_bin[j, i] = 1

# Row-standardize the weights matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    row_sum = W_bin[i].sum()
    if row_sum > 0:
        W[i] = W_bin[i] / row_sum

# Extract change values in the same borough order
delta = df.set_index('borough').reindex(boroughs)['change'].values
z = delta - np.mean(delta)

# Calculate Global Moran's I
numer = float(z @ W @ z)
denom = float(z @ z)
I_obs = numer / denom

# Permutation test: 999 random shuffles
n_perm = 999
np.random.seed(42)
I_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    I_perm[p] = float(z_perm @ W @ z_perm) / denom

# One-sided p-value for positive spatial autocorrelation
p_value = (np.sum(I_perm >= I_obs) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print('N boroughs:', n)
print('Total directed edges:', int(W_bin.sum()))
print('Observed Morans I:', I_obs)
print('One-sided permutation p-value:', p_value)
print('Mean permuted I:', np.mean(I_perm))
print('Std permuted I:', np.std(I_perm))
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_2022_2023_crime.csv'

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Compute change and drop missing
df['change'] = df['Crime_2023'] - df['Crime_2022']
df = df.dropna(subset=['change']).reset_index(drop=True)

boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].tolist())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric binary adjacency matrix
W_bin = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = str(row['borough']).strip()
    b2 = str(row['neighbor']).strip()
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W_bin[i, j] = 1
        W_bin[j, i] = 1

# Row-standardize (isolated boroughs keep zero row)
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    row_sum = W_bin[i].sum()
    if row_sum > 0:
        W[i] = W_bin[i] / row_sum

# Extract change values
delta = df.set_index('borough').reindex(boroughs)['change'].values
z = delta - np.mean(delta)

# Moran's I
numer = float(z @ W @ z)
denom = float(z @ z)
I_obs = numer / denom

# Permutation test (999 shuffles)
n_perm = 999
np.random.seed(42)
I_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    I_perm[p] = float(z_perm @ W @ z_perm) / denom

# Two-sided p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= np.abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print('N boroughs used:', n)
print('Boroughs used:', boroughs)
print('Isolated boroughs (no neighbors):', [boroughs[i] for i in range(n) if W_bin[i].sum() == 0])
print('Observed Morans I:', I_obs)
print('Two-sided permutation p-value:', p_value)
print('Mean permuted I:', np.mean(I_perm))
print('Std permuted I:', np.std(I_perm))
print('Max permuted I:', np.max(I_perm))
print('Min permuted I:', np.min(I_perm))
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_2022_2023_crime.csv'

# Load and clean
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
df['change'] = df['Crime_2023'] - df['Crime_2022']
df = df.dropna(subset=['change']).reset_index(drop=True)

boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].tolist())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Adjacency matrix
W_bin = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = str(row['borough']).strip()
    b2 = str(row['neighbor']).strip()
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i = borough_to_idx[b1]
        j = borough_to_idx[b2]
        W_bin[i, j] = 1
        W_bin[j, i] = 1

# Row-standardize
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    s = W_bin[i].sum()
    if s > 0:
        W[i] = W_bin[i] / s

# Changes
delta = df.set_index('borough').reindex(boroughs)['change'].values
z = delta - np.mean(delta)

# Moran's I
denom = float(z @ z)
I_obs = float(z @ W @ z) / denom

# Permutation test
n_perm = 999
np.random.seed(42)
I_perm = np.empty(n_perm)
for p in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    I_perm[p] = float(z_perm @ W @ z_perm) / denom

# One-sided p-value (positive autocorrelation)
p_one_sided = (np.sum(I_perm >= I_obs) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
# Two-sided for reference
p_two_sided = (np.sum(np.abs(I_perm) >= np.abs(I_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print('Morans I:', I_obs)
print('One-sided p:', p_one_sided)
print('Two-sided p:', p_two_sided)
```
